chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya al-Ajli, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man upon whom was the emancipation of a slave (neck), so he died before he could emancipate a slave. So his son went and bought a slave from his own earnings and emancipated him on behalf of his father. And indeed, the freed slave acquired wealth after that, then died and left it for whoever would be his inheritor.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the emancipation upon his father was for Dhihar (verbal divorce), or thanksgiving, or an obligation upon him, then the freed one is a Sa'ibah (unconditionally freed), there is no right of guardianship for anyone over him. And if he had attached himself (given his Wilayah) before dying to one of the Muslims, and guaranteed his blood-money and his liabilities, he would be his master and his inheritor, if there is no close relative to inherit him.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if he did not attach himself to any of the Muslims until he died, then his inheritance is for the Imam of the Muslims, if there is no close relative to inherit him.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if the emancipation upon his father was voluntary, and his father had instructed him to emancipate a person on his behalf, then the guardianship of the freed one is the inheritance for all the sons of the deceased, from the men.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the one who bought him and emancipated him by the command of his father would be like one of the inheritors, if there is no relative among the free Muslims who would inherit him.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if it was that the son who bought the slave emancipated him on behalf of his father from his own wealth, after the death of his father, voluntarily from himself, without his father having instructed him to do so, then his guardianship and his inheritance is for the one who bought him from his own wealth and emancipated him on behalf of his father, if there is no inheritor for the freed one from his relatives.'

key_terms.سَائِبَةٌ: An unconditionally freed slave who has no master to claim guardianship
key_terms.ظِهَارٌ: A form of pre-Islamic/Islamic verbal divorce
key_terms.عِتْقُ رَقَبَةٍ: Emancipation of a slave (literally: freeing a neck)
key_terms.وَلَاءٌ: Right of guardianship/kinship of the freed slave

ai.seo_question: What are the rules of inheritance for a freed slave when the father's emancipation obligation is fulfilled by the son after the father's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the nuanced jurisprudence of 'Wilayah al-Sa'ibah' (guardianship of the unconditionally freed slave), a key concept in Shia inheritance law where the patron's rights supersede blood relatives. It distinguishes between emancipation for expiation (Kaffarah) or voluntary acts, and whether the son acted under specific instruction or independently, thereby determining if the inheritance reverts to the son, the collective male offspring, or the Imam. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that the act of emancipation creates a proprietary link (Wilayah) that dictates succession in the absence of direct heirs.
